Tasks.Prompt: Given a nonzero segment PQ, first sketch three possible locations that are equally distant from P and Q and write a conjecture about their locus. Then construct the perpendicular bisector with compass and straightedge using two equal-radius arc intersections, label X,Y,M and the right angle, and describe a different valid tracing-paper fold.

Criteria.Criterion: Records three plausible equal-distance placements and describes the provisional perpendicular-bisector conjecture
Draws both intersections X,Y of equal-radius arcs with r>PQ/2 and joins them
Labels midpoint M and right angle, gives equal-radius reason PX=QX, PY=QY
Describes an independent fold placing P on Q and tests both midpoint and perpendicular conditions

Tasks.Accept: Either reflected/rotated or moved diagram; any r>PQ/2, correct two points and teacher-verifiable perpendicularity
Tasks.Reject: Half-radius tangent, one point, eye-only midpoint, typed numeric grade without drawing

Tasks.Prompt: From two distinct points R,S, construct a perpendicular bisector and write why its two constructed points are equidistant from R and S. Compare r=RS/2 and r>RS/2.
Tasks.Exemplar: Draw two circles or arcs from R and S with identical r>RS/2. Mark both crossings X,Y. Join XY, mark M=XY intersection RS and right angle. By equal-radius point membership RX=SX and RY=SY. At r=RS/2 the circles merely touch, yielding only one point.

Criteria.Criterion: Two distinct starting points and two labelled intersections of common arcs
Common opening strictly greater than half the centre separation
Correct line XY and labelled midpoint M/right angle
Equal-distance reason plus correct tangent exception

Tasks.Accept: All correct physical drawings, either side/orientation; exact numerical ruler measurement not required
Tasks.Reject: Treating 1 tangent intersection as a bisector line

SourcePracticeAnalogues.EvidenceMode: Human teacher-reviewed original first-party verbal diagram and paper drawing, not image identical to publisher

Items.Prompt: Take A=(−5,0), B=(5,0), equal circles of radius 6 centred at A and B. The intersections are X,Y and M=(0,0). Decide whether XY is perpendicular to AB, M is midpoint, and AM is perpendicular to MB.
Items.Expected: XY is perpendicular to AB and M is midpoint; AM and MB lie on the same line, so they are not perpendicular. Arc radius is 6>5.

Items.Prompt: Let A=(−3,0), B=(3,0), and E=(−2,4). Is E closer to A or B? Explain with squared distances or geometric position relative to x=0.
Items.Expected: EA²=(1)²+16=17 and EB²=(−5)²+16=41; E is closer to A since its x-coordinate is left of midpoint line x=0.

Items.Prompt: From distinct A,B, specify a valid compass/straightedge construction for an equilateral triangle ABC and justify all three equal sides.
Items.Expected: Draw circles centred A and B, both radius AB; take either intersection C, connect AC,BC; AC=BC=AB.

Items.Prompt: A diagram begins with distinct A,B. Construct intersecting equal-radius arcs from A,B and the complete line through their two intersections X,Y. State the exact condition on r.
Items.Expected: Choose r>AB/2; circles centred A and B with opening r produce two intersections; join X,Y. With r=AB/2 only one point exists.

Items.Prompt: Points A,C,D are collinear with C strictly between A and D; C is centre of a circle through A and D. Point B is on that circle. Which equality must hold: CA=CB, AD=2CA, or AB=BC? Explain.
Items.Expected: CA=CB as radii; AD=CA+CD=2CA since CD=CA; AB=BC is not guaranteed.
